implementation: One thread encloses all eight original weighted contributions and the original shared BF16 merge. A fixed final combined BF16 endpoint removes the original selected contributions as a group, preserving the full unrounded residual. Warp publication and a bounded CTA queue directly emit remaining original indices into the existing window queue. This replaces the old bitmap and duplicate selector scan. Exact replay, expert ordering and production residual combine remain original. The per-invocation owner waits on the recorded same-call shared event and validates counters and guards before freeing storage. It is default off and currently restricted to the qualified q8192 staged/expert-ordered configuration.
correctness_scope: Generated values and expert distributions only. Every safety window queue is checked against the old filter in the standalone fused variant; all four variants check raw route values and complete F32 residual outputs. Full8192 uses256 experts, original staged operands and row flags, expert permutation,16384-block collection windows and bounded replay. Each fixture computes154 periodic CPU dot references and reuses them across selected positions; the report field independent_cpu_dots counts positions checked against those cached references, not independent CPU computations. Repetition across tokens and experts is disclosed. The empirical producer envelope is unchanged and not proved by these tests.
timing_scope: One warmup and three rotated completed host samples per variant in the same executable. Certificate, collection, expert permutation, original replay and production combine are inside; variant3 also includes the actual runtime owner prepare/finish validation. Common allocation, upload/reset, staged operand preparation, row classification, shared-event completion and readback are outside. R1 uses the original default-stream fixture; R6 uses explicit stream ownership and adds the actual runtime helper. Only within-revision comparisons are used. Synthetic component deltas must not be multiplied by40 as measured model TTFT savings.

prior_failures.r2: 30-second prelaunch stream-query deadline; no completed numerical case.
prior_failures.r3: Phase markers localize the same deadline to querying a stream after recording an event, before any comparison kernel.
prior_failures.r4: Explicit nonblocking stream alone does not resolve the prelaunch event-query issue.
prior_failures.r5: Direct event polling resolves the deadline. The first cross-window dense case then exposes the fixture queue reset on the default stream racing the prior nonblocking replay. R6 orders all fixture uploads/readbacks on its owned stream; every case passes.

decision: Keep the default-off integration eligible for same-DLL real-model q8192 GB10 comparison. R6 actual runtime helper saves15.4434ms versus the previous filter in this generated component; no product performance acceptance follows.
